newsitem.title: USA: American General Corp eyes acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: American General Corp eyes acquisitions.

text.p: American General Corp is bidding on a pair of consumer finance units up for sale as part of its plans to expand through acquisitions and internal growth, Chairman Robert Devlin said on Thursday.
The financial services group is bidding on consumer finance operations put up for sale by TransAmerica Corp and BankAmerica Corp, Devlin told reporters after the company's annual meeting here.
"We're looking at a couple of properties that are up for sale in the consumer finance segment," said Devlin, who expects bidding on the units to be completed by late May.

TransAmerica's Los Angeles-based consumer finance unit has about $3.6 billion gross receivables and was put on the blocks in mid-March. BankAmerica has said it expects to sell its unit with loan assets of $1.4 billion by year end.

American General has been taking steps to boost earnings from its consumer finance business, which saw earnings rise 37 percent to $39 million in the first quarter on reduced charge-offs and a $5 million reduction in the allowance for loan losses, the company said.

Devlin, 56, was elected chairman at a board meeting today, succeeding retired Chairman Harold Hook. Devlin retained his title as chief executive officer and James D'Agostino was elected president, the company said.
Devlin said he plans to boost the holding company's market capitalization to $15 billion to $20 billion from about $10 billion following its pending $1.8 billion stock acquisition of USLIFE Corp.
